metadata.title: Micron Stays Flat as 68-Month Bonuses Fail to End Strike Risk

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Record employee payouts did little to defuse Micron Technology's Taiwan labor standoff Friday. Micron (NASDAQ:MU), the memory-chip manufacturer powering AI data centers, traded at $979.37, as local employees prepared to receive rewards worth 35 to 68 months of salary.
The company employs about 15,000 people in Taiwan, representing one-quarter of the more than 60,000 workers receiving fiscal 2026 rewards worldwide. Yet unions representing roughly 10,000 Taiwanese employees are still threatening to strike as they pursue a bonus pool equivalent to 15% of operating profit. The checks are enormous. The dispute is not over.
Micron can afford generosity. Its third-quarter filing reported $41.46 billion in revenue, an 80.4% operating margin and $18.3 billion in adjusted free cash flow, while investment in Taiwan has surpassed T$1.6 trillion. The chart adds a valuation warning: Micron's $979.37 share price stands 55.7% above its $629.03 GF Value estimate. Record rewards may help retain scarce talent, but only a labor agreement can clear the production risk hanging over critical AI-memory supply.
